key_insight: Steady Euler PINNs miss shocks because the loss is too weak, so the paper reformulates shock capturing as a pseudo-time evolution problem that helps shocks emerge gradually.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more robust PINN strategy for transonic/inviscid airfoil flows where shock prediction is critical for aerodynamic design and simulation.
method: Replace steady Euler residuals with unsteady Euler constraints by adding time-derivative terms.
Use pseudo time-stepping in the PDE loss to avoid long-horizon unsteady training issues.
Adopt a simplified Euler formulation to improve shock-capture accuracy.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on four forward problems with different flow conditions and geometries.
watch_item: Training still depends on handling long-time evolution and may be sensitive to the pseudo-time formulation and network optimization settings.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for shock capturing in inviscid flows around an airfoil
